heroHeadline: Day 471: New AJK Assembly Sworn In as PML-N Nears Government Formation; Ceasefire Holds Amid Diplomatic Freeze
heroSubtitle: August 24, 2026: Azad Jammu & Kashmir's 12th Legislative Assembly was sworn in after a final round of reserved-seat polling, capping a drawn-out, violence-marred four-phase 2026 election. PML-N, which won 25 directly-elected seats to PPP's 12, is on track to reach 33 seats with reserved-seat gains and allied support, positioning it to form the next AJK government; speaker/deputy speaker elections follow August 25 and the PM election August 27, with PML-N's Shah Ghulam Qadir and Chaudhry Tariq Farooq both in contention pending Nawaz Sharif's decision. PPP has accused PML-N of rigging and violence in a process shadowed by the JAAC reserved-seat reform protest movement that rights groups say has killed dozens since June. The swearing-in follows a sharper diplomatic week: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal dismissed Pakistan's protest over US Ambassador Sergio Gor's August 19 Kashmir remarks on August 21, and Home Minister Amit Shah's August 17 announcement of the ISI-linked 'Shahzad Bhatti Network' bust drew a 'state-sponsored terrorism' counter-charge from Pakistan's Foreign Office. The ceasefire holds at Day 471 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze remains comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT 'in abeyance,' and Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian aircraft extended to Sept 24.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
